description: Negative-control set for the criterion-degeneracy classifier: 12 degenerate criteria (4 per type) and 12 benign criteria that must not be flagged. Benign samples deliberately include the tricky legitimate cases: 1e-6/1e-9 level consistency, a zero reference whose measured value is also zero, tiny magnitudes whose ratio is well defined, and a one-sided engineering bound.

degenerate.name: reference at the noise floor (Ikeda-type roll damping vs experiment)
degenerate.rationale: |y_ref| = 9e-4 <= 3*sigma = 3e-3: the printed percentage is a property of the noise floor.

degenerate.name: exact zero reference (closure residual vs identity)
degenerate.rationale: y_ref == 0: the relative error is undefined; a printed 3 % tolerance is inapplicable.

degenerate.name: reference absent (self-consistent trend used as benchmark)
degenerate.rationale: No external reference: nothing to divide by, so no relative error exists at all.

degenerate.name: reference far below the engineering scale
degenerate.rationale: |y_ref| = 2e-9 < 0.1*scale = 0.1: the denominator is far below the scale of interest.

degenerate.name: measured and reference have opposite signs (speed-loss style)
degenerate.rationale: sign(y) != sign(y_ref): |Delta|/|y_ref| jumps between +100% and -100% for the same |Delta|.

degenerate.name: sign-sensitive quantity close to zero
degenerate.rationale: flagged sign-sensitive and |y| <= tau*scale: the ratio is dominated by the crossing.

degenerate.name: negative reference, positive measurement
degenerate.rationale: opposite signs: log-ratio undefined, relative error meaningless.

degenerate.name: sign semantics documented in prose only
degenerate.rationale: the quantity is a signed speed change (Delta V<0 means acceleration): the criterion cannot be read as a pure ratio.

degenerate.name: dual standard 3% in header, 10% band in cell
degenerate.rationale: 6% deviation: PASS under the 10 % band, FAIL under the registered 3 %; no priority given.

degenerate.name: reference given as an interval without a priority rule
degenerate.rationale: 56% against the lower bound, 65% against the midpoint: the verdict depends on an unstated choice.

degenerate.name: two tolerances for the same quantity
degenerate.rationale: 4% is inside 5 % and outside 3 %: which one is the criterion?

degenerate.name: reference interval plus a looser band
degenerate.rationale: two degrees of freedom at once; note the merged criterion can still PASS (2.5% < 5%).

benign.name: 1e-9 level agreement
benign.rationale: machine-precision closure, well above the noise floor of a 1.0 reference.

benign.name: zero reference whose measured value is also zero (legitimate)
benign.rationale: |Delta| = 0 is metric-invariant: exact agreement must not be flagged.

benign.name: tiny magnitudes with a well-defined ratio
benign.rationale: the reference is small in absolute terms but not small relative to its own scale (2%).

benign.name: ordinary 0.4% agreement vs a 3% tolerance
benign.rationale: the everyday case that must not be flagged.

benign.name: one-sided engineering bound met (stop distance vs IMO 20L)
benign.rationale: a bound criterion is not an error criterion; excess is 0.

benign.name: signed absolute error inside an engineering tolerance
large magnitudes with 1.9% agreement
benign.rationale: |y_ref| is far above any plausible noise floor.

benign.name: reference comfortably above the noise floor
absolute criterion in engineering units
benign.rationale: 0.2 kN inside 0.5 kN; tolerance and residual share the unit.
